posts.text:
if you can't wear it three years from now, don't buy it. 
stop chasing trends.

boxy fits, heavyweight cotton. 
no logos, just clean lines at strayed.in.

true confidence doesn't need a billboard on your chest. 
prove me wrong.

the bar for how men dress in india is so low that a plain white tee makes you 'the fashion guy'.

we need to talk about this.

oversized fit or structured cut.

you can only pick one for the rest of your life. which one is it?
why does every 'premium' brand mean 4k for a shirt that loses its shape after three washes?

there is always one hoodie in your closet you wear every single time you leave the house.

what’s the one item you can't retire?

we spent four months testing GSM just to get the hang right on our new tees.

check the weight at strayed.in.

everyone talks about the fit of the shirt.
no one talks about how much the collar sags after three washes.

we pulled the white tee from the site for a week.
found a better fabric, but now it’s slightly heavier.
worth it or stick to the original?

two types of guys:
those who wear their best clothes on weekends,
and those who refuse to save anything for later.

nothing beats the look of a worn-in sweater that’s seen a few winters.
brand new is overrated.

waiting for a package to arrive is the most stressful part of online shopping.
anyone else feel that?

a crisp white tee under a blazer is either the best look or trying way too hard.

there is no middle ground.

the most annoying thing about 'premium' clothing is brands charging for the label instead of the fabric weight.

we all know the feeling of a shirt losing its shape after two washes.
it’s always the guy in a plain black hoodie at the airport who looks like he has his life together.

everyone has that one piece of clothing they’ve owned for years that still looks better than anything new they buy.

what is it?

tried to make a logo-heavy piece last month. it felt wrong.

back to keeping things quiet at strayed.in
paying for a brand logo is just paying for the privilege of being a billboard.

ironed shirt vs. wrinkled linen.

there’s no middle ground for a saturday afternoon.
why does every 'premium' heavyweight tee start pilling after three cycles in the wash?

spent six months sourcing a specific cotton weight for our tees.

most people won't notice. the ones who do, stay.
the best flight is the one where you don’t think about what you’re wearing once.

the bar for how men dress in india is so low that a plain white tee makes you 'the fashion guy.'

we need to stop acting like basic fits are a flex.
